title: Actions and Lessons Resulting from SPH Media Trust's Internal Review of Overstated Circulation Numbers
what_it_is: Actions and Lessons Resulting from SPH Media Trust's Internal Review of Overstated Circulation Numbers

sections.label: SPH Media audit questions
sections.summary: Questions ask about timelines for implementing audit recommendations, additional accountability obligations, correction of overstated figures, and Police treatment of a report on overstated circulation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information in respect of the SPH Media Holdings Board’s Audit and Risk Committee findings published on 16 June 2023 (a) what is the timeline for SPH Media Group to implement the recommendations; (b) whether the Ministry will impose additional obligations on the group to tighten accountability; and (c) whether all the overstated circulation figures and consequent financial impact have been corrected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information with respect to SPH Media Group’s filing of a Police report over overstated circulation figures of SPH news publications after potential offences were flagged in an investigation by its audit committee (a) whether the Police has classified the Police report as one that discloses offences for investigation; (b) if so, what are the offences; and (c) how will the Police treat the key investigative findings by SPH Media Group’s audit committee, which include conclusions on the state of knowledge on the part of various SPH officers in relation to the inflated circulation numbers.

sections.label: SPH Media funding questions
sections.summary: Questions ask whether S$900 million funding continues, how prudence is ensured, whether funds were disbursed and reassessed, and if KPIs cover risk culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information in view of the report released by the Audit and Risk Committee of SPH Media Holdings Pte Ltd (a) whether the Ministry still plans to continue its S$900 million funding support for SPH Media Trust over the next five years; and (b) how will the Ministry ensure that such monies are spent prudently with good accountability and oversight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) whether the Government's funding agreement with SPH Media Trust has been concluded and if any funds have been disbursed; (b) if so, whether these funds will be re-assessed in light of the report of the Audit and Risk Committee of SPH Media released on 16 June 2023; and (c) whether the key performance indicators for the funding agreement will include evaluations of SPH Media Trust's risk culture and improvements to its risk management practices and internal controls and processes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The first is that the events took place before SMT was formed, when the media business was under SPH Limited (SPHL), a privately listed company.

sections.label: Overstated circulation numbers
sections.summary: The overstatement of circulation numbers amounted to around 82,600 average daily copies at August 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: First, the overstatement of circulation numbers amounted to around 82,600 average daily copies at August 2021.

sections.label: Financial year 2021 findings
sections.summary: For the year ending August 2021, profits were understated by about S$110,000, with inconsistent circulation reporting, improper revenue accounting and a questionable barter deal.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For the financial year ending August 2021, there was approximately S$110,000 in understatement of profits.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Circulation numbers had been reported in a manner inconsistent with established standards, there was improper accounting of revenue and there was a barter deal which was possibly a questionable arrangement, entered into for the sole purpose of inflating circulation numbers.

sections.label: Print news consumption drop
sections.summary: In the same Reuters Institute report, the share of respondents consuming print news dropped to 22% from 53% six years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the same report by Reuters Institute, the share of respondents who consume print news has dropped to 22%, from 53% just six years ago.

sections.label: Government continues funding SMT
sections.summary: MCI will work with SMT on disruption and transformation, and the Government will continue funding SMT at committed amounts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: MCI is committed to working with SMT to overcome the challenges of disruption and succeed in its transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Therefore, to Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Leong Mun Wai's questions, the Government will continue funding SMT at the amounts we committed to.

sections.label: Funding agreement accountability measures
sections.summary: The March funding agreement includes measures requiring SMT to submit KPI information, including methodologies and sources.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To assure Members, the funding agreement concluded in March this year already contains measures to ensure accountability, for example: (a) SMT is required to submit specific information on KPIs, including their methodologies and sources.

sections.label: MCI mid-term funding review
sections.summary: MCI will review the funding agreement's terms, including KPIs and funding quantum, at the mid-term juncture.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: MCI will also be reviewing the terms of the funding agreement, including the KPIs and funding quantum, at the mid-term juncture.

sections.label: Circulation metric no longer relevant
sections.summary: The speaker said circulation is a metric that is no longer as relevant, as explained in February 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As I explained to Members in February 2023 during the Parliament Sitting and in response to Members' questions, and as I have also alluded to earlier in my response, circulation is a metric that is no longer as relevant.

sections.label: KPIs total reach and engagement
sections.summary: The funding arrangement's KPIs include total reach and engagement of SMT's products, focusing on digital platforms for digital transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The KPIs, therefore, that we have included in the funding arrangement include the total reach and engagement of SMT's full range of products, with a focus on their digital platforms, because we have to keep in mind that the whole purpose for funding SMT is to ensure that the digital transformation is successful.

sections.label: KPI reports and funding impact
sections.summary: SMT must submit regular independently audited KPI reports, and unmet KPI targets will impact the funding amount.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: SMT is required to submit regular reports on their KPI performance, which must also be independently audited, as I mentioned earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And if the KPI targets are not met, the amount of funding will be impacted.

sections.label: Funding disbursement and Police action
sections.summary: The Government began disbursing funds to SMT in March 2023 before the ARC completed findings, and further action is for the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Two, can the Minister confirm that the Ministry is not pursuing the responsibility of the past top management of SPH Limited at the moment?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I can confirm that the Government started disbursing funds to SMT in March 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: At the time, the ARC had not completed its findings.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But the important point to note is that by March 2023, only then, funding arrangements with SMT started, whereas the events in question took place well before March 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The second question is whether there will be further action taken against those who had been involved in this incident.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: That is a matter for the Police to decide.

sections.label: Board circulation numbers overstatement scale
sections.summary: The Board intended to establish the scale of overstated circulation numbers, and the speaker is unaware of terms of reference asking the ARC to investigate before September 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The intention of the Board was to establish the scale of the circulation numbers being overstated.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I am not aware of the terms of reference asking for the ARC to investigate the matter before September 2020.

sections.label: No funding relationship before ARC investigation
sections.summary: The speaker says there was no funding relationship before the period investigated by the ARC, questions the reason for such an investigation, and says accountability must be clear going forward.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I did not answer one part of the question.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I think I have to remind Members that we did not have a funding relationship with them before the period that was being investigated by the ARC.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: What reason do we have to ask for an investigation of that nature?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But going forward, henceforth, that is where the accountability has to be very clear.
